sec: Hyponatremia · euvolemic typing, SIADH criteria, causes and CSW versus SIADH

items.q: Assess the two pyramids drawn on Book p963: I The vomiting pyramid pairs hyponatremia and hypokalemia with alkalosis. II The diarrhea pyramid, illustrated with VIPoma, pairs them with a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis.
items.exp: Vomiting gives hyponatremia + hypokalemia + alkalosis, whereas diarrhea (VIPoma) gives hypokalemia with acidosis, annotated NAGMA for normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. (Book p963)

items.q: Each abnormality below completes one of the two triangles on this page EXCEPT:
items.exp: Both triangles carry hyponatremia and hypokalemia, with alkalosis in vomiting and NAGMA in diarrhea; potassium is never raised in either. (Book p963)

items.q: A 41-year-old woman has 5 weeks of secretory diarrhea; sodium 132 mEq/L, potassium 2.7 mEq/L, pH 7.31 with a normal anion gap. A VIPoma is suspected. Which combination does the diarrhea triangle on this page predict?
items.exp: The diarrhea (VIPoma) triangle is drawn with hyponatremia, hypokalemia and acidosis labelled NAGMA, exactly the picture in this patient. (Book p963)

items.q: A euvolemic patient with hyponatremia is being worked up for SIADH. Which pair of deficiencies must the page have you rule out first?
items.exp: The euvolemic algorithm is a single step: rule out cortisol/thyroid hormone insufficiency, and only then call the picture SIADH. (Book p963)

items.q: Match each SIADH criterion with the direction or cut-off given — 1) Serum osmolality 2) Urine osmolality 3) Urine sodium … A) Decreased B) Increased, greater than serum C) Increased, above 20 mEq/l
items.exp: The criteria are reduced serum osmolality, urine osmolality higher than serum, and urine Na+ above 20 mEq/l, together with clinical euvolemia and absence of other disease. (Book p963)

items.q: What urine sodium cut-off is written into the SIADH criteria on this page?
items.exp: Criterion four is a doubled urine Na+ of more than 20 mEq/l, reflecting the natriuresis of euvolemia. (Book p963)

items.q: Assess two SIADH criteria: I Clinical euvolemia is explained as the effect of increased ANF with an unstimulated renin-angiotensin system. II The last criterion requires the presence of pituitary, adrenal, thyroid, renal or liver disease.
items.exp: Euvolemia is attributed to increased ANF plus a negative RAS; the fifth criterion is the ABSENCE of pituitary, adrenal, thyroid, renal or liver disease, not its presence. (Book p963)

items.q: A patient with cirrhosis has a serum sodium of 128 mEq/L with urine Na+ 8 mEq/L. Which SIADH criterion does this patient fail?
items.exp: SIADH may only be diagnosed when pituitary, adrenal, thyroid, renal and liver disease are all absent, and cirrhosis also produces a hypervolemic hyponatremia with low urine sodium. (Book p963)

items.q: Match each SIADH cause category with the examples listed under it — 1) Trauma 2) Paraneoplastic 3) Infections … A) Necrotising pneumonia, meningo-encephalitis B) Head injury C) Small cell carcinoma of lung, pancreatic cancer, duodenal malignancy, lymphoma
items.exp: Trauma lists head injury, paraneoplastic lists small cell carcinoma of lung, pancreatic cancer, duodenal malignancy and lymphoma, and infections list necrotising pneumonia and meningo-encephalitis. (Book p963)

items.q: All of these tumours appear in the paraneoplastic list for SIADH EXCEPT:
items.exp: The paraneoplastic list names small cell carcinoma of lung, pancreatic cancer, duodenal malignancy and lymphoma; squamous lung cancer is not included. (Book p963)

items.q: Fill up: The five drug causes of SIADH grouped as the '5 C's' are chlorpropamide, chlorpromazine, cyclophosphamide, ______ and ______.
items.exp: The 5 C's are chlorpropamide, chlorpromazine, cyclophosphamide, carbamazepine and clofibrate. (Book p963)

items.q: Which agent appears in the 'Others' drug list for SIADH rather than among the 5 C's?
items.exp: The Others list holds oxytocin, nicotine, NSAIDs, psychiatric drugs and vincristine; the other three are members of the 5 C's. (Book p963)

items.q: A 58-year-old on ABVD chemotherapy for lymphoma has sodium 119 mEq/L, serum osmolality 258 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 520 mOsm/kg and urine Na+ 46 mEq/L, with normal cortisol and thyroid profiles. Which listed drug mechanism best explains this?
opts: SIADH from a drug in the 'Others' list
Thiazide action on the distal convoluted tubule
Cerebral salt wasting after nodal infiltration
items.exp: Drugs are a named SIADH category on this page, with vincristine in the Others list; the biochemical pattern satisfies all five SIADH criteria. (Book p963)

items.q: Assess the CSW and SIADH comparison table: I CSW is described as hypovolemic with an increased serum potassium. II A raised brain natriuretic peptide is entered in the SIADH column, opposite a dash in the CSW column.
items.exp: CSW is the hypovolemic column with increased serum K+ and increased BNP; SIADH is euvolemic with normal serum K+, and BNP carries a dash in the SIADH column. (Book p963)

items.q: Below which serum uric acid value does the SIADH column of the CSW versus SIADH table place its doubled fall?
items.exp: Both columns record a fall in serum uric acid, but only SIADH quantifies it as below 4 mg/dl. (Book p963)

items.q: Fill up: The first row of the comparison table attributes CSW to a loss of ______ tone, entered with a negative ______ entry, while the SIADH column simply carries a dash.
items.exp: The CSW entry reads loss of adrenergic tone with a negative RAS, a distinction not made for SIADH, which is left as a dash. (Book p963)

items.q: Six days after a craniotomy a patient has sodium 121 mEq/L, urine output 4 L/day, tachycardia, a collapsed IVC and urine Na+ 90 mEq/L. Which immediate step does the CSW pattern demand?
opts: Isotonic saline replacement for the hypovolaemia
Start tolvaptan after checking liver function
Give desmopressin to curb the natriuresis
items.exp: Cerebral salt wasting is the hypovolemic column of the table, so the priority is volume repletion with saline; fluid restriction and vaptans are treatments aimed at euvolemic SIADH. (Book p963)

items.q: Patients from all of these groups are listed as prone to develop hyponatremia with seizures EXCEPT:
items.exp: The three seizure-prone groups named are psychogenic polydipsia, post-traumatic or head injury patients, and post-operative patients. (Book p963)
